title: What is Long? What is Round?

learn.hook: A snake and a worm went for a walk. Who is longer?
points: Long things stretch a big way from end to end.
Short things stretch only a little way.
To compare, put both ends at the same start line.
Longest means more long than all others. Shortest means less long than all.

example.q: Riya has a pencil and a crayon. Both start at the same line. The pencil ends farther. Which is longer?
steps: Line up one end of both.

learn.reallife: A train is long. A toffee is short. A plait can be long or short.

games.title: Shortest to longest
games.prompt: Put them from shortest to longest

games.title: True or false?
items: A train is longer than a car.
A train has many coaches. It is very long.
A spoon is longer than a bed.
A bed is much longer than a spoon.
To compare length, start both things at the same line.
Then the one that ends farther is longer.
An eraser is longer than a cricket bat.
A cricket bat is much longer.
A giraffe's neck is longer than a cat's tail.
A giraffe has a very long neck.

quiz.q: Which is longer?
quiz.explain: A cricket bat is much longer than a tiny matchstick.

quiz.q: Which is the shortest?
quiz.explain: A paper clip is the shortest of the three.
quiz.mistake: Picks the longest instead of the shortest

quiz.q: Meena's ribbon is long. Aisha's ribbon is short. Whose ribbon is longer?
quiz.explain: Long is more than short. So Meena's ribbon is longer.

quiz.q: Two sticks start at the same line. Stick A ends first. Which is shorter?
quiz.explain: The stick that ends first does not go as far. So Stick A is shorter.

quiz.q: Which animal has a long trunk?
quiz.explain: Only the elephant has a trunk. It is long!
quiz.mistake: Does not know which animal has a trunk

quiz.q: Kabir lays a pen next to a ruler. The ruler is longer. Which is shorter?
quiz.explain: If the ruler is longer, the pen must be shorter.
quiz.mistake: Gets confused between longer and shorter

teach.ask: Gappu: My worm and my pencil look the same. How do I know which is longer?
teach.praise: Clever! Line them up and see which goes farther!
teach.nudge: Should I put them at the same start? Which word tells me long or short?

learn.hook: A ball and a plate are at a party. Which can bounce away?
points: Round things have curved sides, like a ball.
Flat things have flat faces, like a book.
A ball is round all over. It has no flat face.
Some things have both, like a tin can. Its sides are curved. Its top is flat.

example.q: Is a dice round or flat?
steps: All its faces are flat squares.

learn.reallife: A laddoo and a ball are round. A book and a carrom board are flat.

quiz.q: Which one is round all over?
quiz.explain: A ball is curved everywhere. Books and bricks have flat faces.

quiz.q: Which one has flat faces?
quiz.explain: A dice has 6 flat faces. Oranges and marbles are round.

quiz.q: A square gift box is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A box with square faces is like a cube.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every solid is a sphere

quiz.q: A sheet of paper is flat. Which is also flat?
quiz.explain: A notebook cover is flat like the paper. A laddoo and a ball are round.

quiz.q: A tin of ghee has curved sides. What shape is it like?
quiz.explain: A tin has a curved side and two flat round ends. That is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all curved things are spheres

quiz.q: Joseph's birthday cap is pointy at the top. It is like a ___.
quiz.explain: A birthday cap has a round bottom and a point on top. That is a cone.

teach.ask: Gappu: I found a ball and a book. Are they the same shape?
teach.praise: Yes! A ball is round. A book is flat!
teach.nudge: Which one is round? Which one is flat?

topics.title: Round things, long things, box shapes

learn.hook: A bangle and a ladder are very different. Can you tell how?
points: Round things like a bangle or a coin go in the circle box.
Long things like a pencil or a ladder go in the long rectangle box.
A matchbox has flat faces and corners. A brick and a lunch box have the same shape.
Things with the same shape match, even if size or colour is different.

example.q: Which one has the same shape as a matchbox: a brick, a ball or a birthday cap?
steps: A matchbox has flat faces and corners.
A brick also has flat faces and corners.
A ball is round. A cap is pointy.

learn.reallife: A lunch box, a shoe box and a brick all have the matchbox shape.

quiz.q: Which thing has the same shape as a matchbox?
quiz.explain: A brick has flat faces and corners, just like a matchbox.
quiz.mistake: Does not match shapes by their faces

quiz.q: Riya draws a bangle. Which box should it go in?
quiz.explain: A bangle is round. Round things go in the circle box.

quiz.q: Kabir draws a ladder. Which box should it go in?
quiz.explain: A ladder is long. Long things go in the rectangle box.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT shaped like a box?
quiz.explain: A ball is round all over. A brick and a matchbox are box shapes.

quiz.q: Meena has a small ball and a big football. Do they have the same shape?
options: Yes, both are round like a ball
quiz.explain: Size does not change shape. Both are round all over.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a different size means a different shape

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a matchbox have?
quiz.explain: Top, bottom and 4 sides. That is 6 faces.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the top and bottom faces

teach.ask: Gappu: Is a brick like a ball or like a matchbox? Where do I draw a bangle?
teach.praise: Brick like a matchbox, bangle in the circle box. Super!
teach.nudge: Does a brick have flat faces or is it round?

learn.hook: Let us build a house, a tower and a robot with things from home!
points: We can build with boxes, books, bottles, caps and funnels.
Boxes and books have flat faces. They stack well.
Balls are round all over. They roll off a stack.
A cone or a cap sits well on top, like a roof.
Tell the shapes you used: 'I used two boxes and a cap.'

example.q: Aisha builds a tower: a big box, a small box and a cone on top. Why does it stand?
steps: Boxes have flat faces. One sits flat on the other.
The cone has a flat bottom, so it sits on the box.
Its pointy top must go last.
example.answer: Flat faces stack, and the cone goes on top

learn.reallife: Builders use bricks with flat faces to make strong walls.

games.title: Builder's true or false
items: Books are good for the bottom of a tower.
A ball is good for the bottom of a tower.
It is round and rolls away.
A cone can be the roof of a toy house.
Its pointy top looks like a roof.
A box will stay on the tip of a cone.
The tip is pointed. The box will fall.
Bottle caps can be wheels of a toy bus.

quiz.q: Joseph wants a tall tower. Which is best to stack?
quiz.explain: Boxes have flat faces. They sit on each other without rolling.

quiz.q: Why does a ball fall off a stack?
quiz.explain: A ball has no flat face to sit on, so it rolls off.
quiz.mistake: Does not link round shape with rolling

quiz.q: Riya makes a toy house from a box. What can be its roof?
quiz.explain: A cone has a flat bottom and a pointy top, like a roof.
quiz.mistake: Picks a round thing that will roll off

quiz.q: Kabir makes a bus from a box. Which can be its wheels?
quiz.explain: Bottle caps are round like wheels.
quiz.mistake: Does not see which shape is like a wheel

quiz.q: Meena stacks 3 books. She puts 1 box on top. How many things are in her stack?
quiz.explain: 3 books and 1 box make 4 things.

quiz.q: Aisha says, 'My robot has a box for a body and two glasses for legs.' What is she doing?
quiz.explain: She names the shapes in her model.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the shape words

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to build a tall tower. Should I use balls or boxes?
teach.praise: Flat boxes stack, round balls roll. Gappu's tower is tall!
teach.nudge: What happens if I put a ball on top? Why?

learn.hook: Push a ball and push a book. What happens?
points: Round things can roll, like a ball or a bangle.
Things with flat faces slide when we push them.
A cylinder can roll on its side. It slides on its flat end.
A cube cannot roll. It can only slide.

example.q: Can a tin of biscuits roll and slide?
steps: Lay the tin on its curved side. Push. It rolls.
Stand it on its flat end. Push. It slides.
example.answer: Yes, it can roll and slide.

learn.reallife: Wheels roll on the road. A cupboard slides when we push it.

games.title: True or false?
items: A ball is round all over. It rolls easily.
A book can roll down a slope.
A book has flat faces. It slides.
A tin can roll on its curved side.
The curved side lets it roll.
A dice rolls smoothly like a ball.
A dice has flat faces. It tumbles but does not roll smoothly.
A cylinder can slide on its flat end.
Its flat end sits flat, so it can slide.

quiz.q: Which one rolls?
quiz.explain: A marble is round. Round things roll.

quiz.q: Which one will slide, not roll?
quiz.explain: A box has flat faces. It slides.

quiz.q: Why can a bicycle wheel roll?
quiz.explain: Round things roll. A wheel is round.

quiz.q: Arjun pushes a cube. What does it do?
quiz.explain: A cube has flat faces. It slides.

quiz.q: Which can roll on one side and slide on another?
quiz.explain: A tin rolls on its curved side. It slides on its flat end.
quiz.mistake: Picks something that does only one

quiz.q: Aisha wants a toy that rolls down a slide. Which should she pick?
quiz.explain: A ball is round, so it rolls down.

teach.ask: Gappu: Why does my ball roll away but my book stays?
teach.praise: Now I know! Round things roll. Flat things slide!
teach.nudge: What shape is the ball? What does a flat thing do?

learn.hook: Let us test! Push it and see: does it roll, slide or do both?
points: Write R if a thing rolls. Write S if it slides.
Some things do both. A bottle rolls on its side and slides on its bottom.
Test it: push it on the floor or let it go down a slope.
Tick ✓ what it can do. Cross ✗ what it cannot do.

example.q: Test a bottle cap. Does it roll, slide or both?
steps: Stand it on its round edge and push. It rolls.
Lay it flat and push. It slides.

learn.reallife: On the playground, a ball rolls down the slide. You slide down it!

items.text: A bottle can roll and also ___.
A book on a slope will ___.

quiz.q: Riya writes R or S. What should she write for a football?
quiz.explain: A football rolls. R means rolls.

quiz.q: What should Riya write for a brick?
quiz.explain: A brick has flat faces. It slides, so S.

quiz.q: Which can roll and slide both?
quiz.explain: A bottle rolls on its curved side and slides on its flat bottom.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that one thing can do both

quiz.q: Kabir pushes an eraser on the floor. What does it do?
quiz.explain: An eraser has flat faces. It slides.

quiz.q: Joseph tests: ball rolls ✓, book ✗, glass rolls ✓, box ✗. How many things can roll?
quiz.explain: Ball and glass got a tick. That is 2.

quiz.q: A tin can rolls on its side. Can it also slide?
quiz.explain: Stand it on its flat end and push. It slides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a round thing can never slide

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know if a bottle rolls, slides or does both?
teach.praise: Push and test! A bottle does both. Wow!
teach.nudge: What happens on its curved side? And on its flat bottom?
